name: Curation

subjectOf.text: The apparent abundance of internet text overstates the usable supply, because much of it fails quality thresholds for model training due to redundancy, noise, or irrelevance.
subjectOf.abstract: while the internet contains a vast corpus of textual material, not all content meets quality thresholds suitable for model training, given issues such as redundancy, noise, or irrelevance.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Artificial Intelligence The Final Frontier (2025). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=5095633
scope_conditions: applies to internet-sourced text used for model training

subjectOf.text: Ferbach et al. (2024) report that curation acts as implicit preference optimization that amplifies the curator's biases.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: The finding is prior work cited by the paper and is not measured in this study.
It is the channel the parent reputation program claims reputation can resist.

description: 2 claims in the published works of Wulf A. Kaal carry the concept tag 'curation'. Derived node: a roster, not an adjudicated definition.
